notice: SYNTHETIC HELP CENTER — written for the AgentDesk demo. Every article describes behaviour the AgentDesk code really has (see README); none of it comes from a real support team or real customers.

articles.title: Why am I seeing "Too many requests" (HTTP 429)?

sections.heading: Rate limits
sections.content: Typed questions, the comparison narrative and voice input spend model credit, so they are rate limited. Each connection may ask 10 questions and request 10 narratives per 10 minutes, and send 20 voice clips per 10 minutes. All three share one budget of 300 model calls per UTC day. When a limit is reached the request returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header that says how many seconds remain in the window.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.content: Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again. The sample question chips do not count against the limit because they show pre-verified saved answers. Product comparison and the review queue are never rate limited.

articles.title: Why does a typed question take so long?

sections.heading: Answer latency
sections.content: A typed question runs the live pipeline: retrieval, a grounded draft and a citation check on every quote. Measured on 2026-11-17, typed questions took 28 to 76 seconds end to end, with a median of 33 seconds. The page says so while it works. The five sample question chips answer instantly because they are pre-verified saved answers.

articles.title: Why did the assistant say "Insufficient evidence"?

sections.heading: Refusals
sections.content: When the product documents do not contain the answer, the assistant refuses instead of guessing and shows INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. It still cites what the documents do say and lists exactly what is missing. Asking which product is best is stopped by a deterministic rule before any model is called, because AgentDesk never makes a final recommendation.

articles.title: How do I check a citation against the PDF?

sections.heading: Citation cards
sections.content: Every factual claim carries a citation card with the document name, the page number and the exact English sentence. The link on the card opens the PDF at that page. Every quote is checked by code to be an exact substring of the retrieved passage, and the page number is attached by code, not by the model.

articles.title: How do I compare two products?

sections.heading: Comparison drafts
sections.content: Open Product Comparison, choose two different products and, optionally, a demo client. The 13-row fact table is generated by code and every factual cell links to a document page and quote. A cell can be available, not applicable, not provided or conflict. AgentDesk never ranks the two products and has no score or winner field.

articles.title: How do I send a comparison for review?

sections.heading: Review workflow
sections.content: From a comparison draft, choose Send for review. The reviewer sees a frozen snapshot of the facts as they were when the review was created. A review can be approved, rejected or sent back with a revision request, and each decision is added to an append-only audit trail. Sending the same comparison again while a review is still pending opens the existing review instead of creating a second one.

sections.heading: Voice questions
sections.content: Press the microphone, speak your question, then review the transcript before sending it yourself. A transcript is never submitted automatically, because Chinese insurance terms are sometimes transcribed wrongly and a person should confirm the text first.

articles.title: Do I need an account or a password?

sections.heading: Access
sections.content: The AgentDesk demo has no login, no accounts and no passwords. Anyone with the link can open it. There is nothing to reset, and support will never ask you for a password.

articles.title: What does Run automation do after a review?

sections.heading: Follow-up tasks
sections.content: After a review is approved or sent back for revision, Run automation creates one internal follow-up task. It never contacts a client: the task has no recipient field. When no webhook is configured the result is labelled Demo / mock, which means nothing was sent. Rejected reviews create no task.

sections.heading: Fictional data
sections.content: No. Every product, carrier, rate and client in AgentDesk is fictional, and every PDF page is stamped DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT — FICTIONAL PRODUCT — NOT FOR SALE. Nothing in the app is a quote, a policy illustration or a suitability determination.
